newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian guards accused of killing 104 officials.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian guards accused of killing 104 officials.

text.p: Former guards of Ethiopia's ousted Marxist ruler were charged on Thursday with killing 104 officials including an array of high-ranking leaders 23 years ago.

The former head of guards for Marxist ruler Mengistu Haile Mariam and two colleagues were charged with killing a navy admiral, who was a grandson of the late Emperor Haile Selassie, a cousin of the emperor, three former prime ministers, 19 generals, 25 ministers and many other top government officials.

Prosecutors said Colonel Sileshi Mekuria, Warrant Officer Lemma Kumsa, Corporal Wubeshet Adera and Private Gezahegn Bekele committed the killings in 1974 when the emperor was overthrown by the military.
Three of the accused were in the court in Addis Ababa on Thursday and the fourth, Lemma, is on trial in absentia.
Sileshi and the other three were also charged with killing Brigadier-General Teferi Benti, chairman of the military junta known as the Dergue, and six officials in 1977 for opposing Mengistu.

Prosecutors said Sileshi and his accomplices also murdered 36 people accused of belonging to an opposition Marxist cell in 1978 and 1979. Mengistu emerged the most powerful Dergue member in 1975 and was ousted in 1991. He lives in exile in Zimbabwe.

Sileshi in 1990 was brought from prison and identified where the remains of the emperor, who was killed in 1975, had been hidden under the floor of a toilet in the grounds of the former imperial palace in Addis Ababa.
A total of 71 former Dergue officials are on trial charged with genocide and crimes against humanity. Only 46 are in the dock with the other 25 including Mengistu on trial in absentia.
